subtitle: How a wandering son of the soil crowned a king with words

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view of a dusty road turning into a royal camp, with Banabhatta in foreground holding a palm-leaf manuscript, Harsha’s distant pavilion glowing under dusk
panels.action: Banabhatta stands at the edge of Harsha's vast war camp, clutching a bundle of palm leaves, as lines of tents and banners stretch into the fading light beyond him.

dialogue.text: In Harsha’s roaring age of conquest, a poor wanderer named Banabhatta walked into the king’s camp—and turned power into prose that still troubles historians today.

i18n.hi: हर्ष के धधकते विजयकाल में, बनभट्ट नाम का गरीब भटकन राजा के शिविर में जा घुसा—और ताकत को ऐसी गद्य में बदला जो आज भी इतिहासकारों को परेशान रखती है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high, showing a riverside village fading into fields, with a boy Banabhatta and his father near a modest hut
panels.action: Young Banabhatta sits beside his father on a reed mat outside a humble house, listening as the older man traces letters in the dust near a quiet riverbank.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta later begins his own tale far from courts, in a village by the Ganga, learning letters from a father whose life, like so many, will end before the story truly starts.

i18n.hi: बनभट्ट अपनी कहानी शुरू करता है दरबारों से दूर, गंगा किनारे गाँव में, जहाँ वो उन अक्षरों से जूझता है जो पिता सिखा रहे हैं—जिनकी ज़िंदगी, औरों की तरह, असली कहानी शुरू होने से पहले ही खत्म हो जाएगी।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot, low light inside the hut, with Banabhatta’s father lying still and Bana seated nearby, the world outside blurred
panels.action: Inside the dim hut, Banabhatta sits motionless by the straw bed where his father lies lifeless, a small oil lamp casting long shadows on the mud walls.

dialogue.text: In his Harshacharita, Bana tells of his father’s death and the sudden emptiness that followed, the village shrinking, the world turning cold around one small orphaned house.

i18n.hi: ‘हर्षचरित’ में बना पिता की मौत और अचानक आई सूनी खामोशी लिखता है, सिमटता गाँव, ठंडी पड़ती दुनिया, और बीच में पड़ा उसका छोटा, अनाथ सा घर।

panels.shot: wide tracking shot along a dusty road, Banabhatta moving with a cloth bag and staff, villages and groves passing behind him
panels.action: Banabhatta walks along a sun-baked country road with a staff and a small bundle, passing groves, shrines, and scattered huts as birds circle over the fields.

dialogue.text: He wanders. Through villages and groves, among strangers and kin, the young Brāhman becomes a wayfarer, his own prose later remembering hunger, odd kindnesses, and the long road north.

i18n.hi: वो निकल पड़ता है। गाँवों, उपवनों, अनजानों और रिश्तेदारों के बीच भटकते हुए, यह जवान ब्राह्मण राहगीर बन जाता है—उसकी गद्य बाद में भूख, अजीब नेकी और उत्तर की लंबी राह को याद करती है।

panels.shot: crowded bazaar wide shot, slightly elevated, with Bana seated near a tree reciting to a few listeners amid merchants and animals
panels.action: In a bustling market town, Banabhatta sits beneath a tree, gesturing with his hand as a small circle of listeners lean in while merchants and cattle move around them.

dialogue.text: Bana polishes his tongue in markets and rest-houses, stringing ornate phrases, learning how people listen, how kings are praised and mocked by word of mouth.

i18n.hi: बाज़ारों और सरायों में बन अपनी ज़ुबान को चमकाता है, भारी-भरकम वाक्य गढ़ते हुए, सीखता है लोग कैसे सुनते हैं, और राजाओं की वाहवाही और चुगली ज़ुबान से ज़ुबान कैसे घूमती है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a modest noble residence, with Krishna’s emissary speaking to Bana; focus on Bana’s startled face
panels.action: In the courtyard of a provincial mansion, Banabhatta looks up in surprise as a finely dressed emissary addresses him, other attendants watching from the veranda.

dialogue.text: Then, in his own telling, a summons: Harsha’s kinsman Krishna hears of this sharp-tongued wanderer and calls him, a stray word about a stray poet drifting into royal circles.

i18n.hi: फिर, उसकी ही ज़ुबानी, बुलावा आता है: हर्ष का संबंधी कृष्ण इस नुकीली ज़ुबान वाले घुमक्कड़ के बारे में सुनता है और उसे बुला भेजता है—भटका कवि, भटकी खबर बनकर राज-दरबार में जा पहुँचता है।

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Krishna’s presence implied off-frame, with Bana bowing deeply, a mix of awe and calculation on his face
panels.action: Banabhatta bows before an unseen noble seated on a raised platform, his hands folded, eyes lifted just enough to show both respect and keen curiosity.

dialogue.speaker: banabhatta
dialogue.text: If I have any gift, lord, it is only this restless tongue.

i18n.hi: यदि मुझे कोई वरदान मिला है स्वामी, तो बस यह बेचैन ज़ुबान ही है।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye shot dissolving into a caravan scene, showing the journey from countryside towards Harsha’s encampment near Kannauj
panels.action: A caravan of horses, ox-carts, and armed escorts moves across a river plain, with Banabhatta riding among them, looking ahead toward a distant cluster of royal tents.

dialogue.text: From Krishna’s side, Bana is drawn toward the greater sun—Harsha himself. His own prose makes the journey shimmer with omens, but the reality is clear: a poet is being recruited.

i18n.hi: कृष्ण की छाँव से उठकर बना बड़े सूरज की तरफ खिंचता है—स्वयं हर्ष की ओर। उसकी अपनी गद्य इस सफर को शकुनों से जगमग दिखाती है, पर सच्चाई साफ है: एक कवि की भर्ती हो रही है।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Harsha’s sprawling camp at Pritikuta, flags and elephants, with Bana’s caravan arriving at the edge
panels.action: Harsha’s vast war camp sprawls along the riverbank at Pritikuta, rows of tents, elephants, and watchfires stretching out as Banabhatta’s small party halts at the outskirts.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta places himself at Pritikuta, at Harsha’s encampment, where the king of Kannauj and Thanesar coordinates war and diplomacy under a forest of banners.

i18n.hi: बनभट्ट खुद को प्रीतिकूट में रखता है, हर्ष के शिविर में, जहाँ कन्नौज और थानेसर का राजा झंडों के जंगल तले युद्ध और सुलह की डोरें खींचता है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot inside a large command tent, with courtiers around and Bana placed before an empty throne space, waiting
panels.action: Inside a grand tent lined with carpets and spears, Banabhatta stands before a low platform reserved for the king, courtiers to either side watching the newcomer with measured interest.

dialogue.text: He waits in the king’s pavilion, surrounded by Harsha’s officers and scribes. Somewhere beyond the canvas walls lies the man he will immortalise in words.

i18n.hi: वह राजा के मंडप में इंतज़ार करता है, चारों ओर हर्ष के अफ़सर और लेखक। कपड़े की दीवारों के उस पार कहीं वह आदमी बैठा है जिसे वो शब्दों में अमर करने आया है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot from behind Bana, as Harsha enters implied in the frame’s light, Bana’s shoulders tense slightly
panels.action: Banabhatta, seen from behind, straightens as the tent flap is lifted and a royal figure steps in, his silhouette framed by bright daylight from outside.

dialogue.text: In the Harshacharita, the king’s entry is wrapped in hyperbole—Harsha as god-like ruler—but scholars today read through that glowing veil to see a human sovereign needing praise.

i18n.hi: ‘हर्षचरित’ में राजा की एंट्री बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर लिपटी है—हर्ष, देव जैसे शासक के रूप में—पर आज के विद्वान उस चमकती नकाब के पार एक इंसानी सम्राट को देखते हैं, जिसे सराहना की ज़रूरत है।

panels.shot: tight mid-shot on Bana reciting, one hand raised, courtiers listening; focus on his expressive face
panels.action: Banabhatta stands with one hand lifted, reciting with intense concentration as seated courtiers lean forward, their expressions shifting from doubt to intrigue.

dialogue.speaker: banabhatta
dialogue.text: May my poor words be a garland fit for a lion among kings.

i18n.hi: मेरे गँवार शब्द भी राजाओं के सिंह के गले की माला बन जाएँ।

panels.shot: close-up on Harsha’s implied hand rewarding Bana, placing a necklace or cloth, with Bana’s bowed head in foreground
panels.action: A royal hand reaches out to place an ornate cloth over Banabhatta’s bowed shoulders, his face partly visible, eyes lowered, jaw tight with emotion.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta’s own narrative hints at royal favour: the wanderer becomes court poet, lifted suddenly into the inner circle that frames Harsha’s image for the world.

i18n.hi: बनभट्ट की अपनी कथा राज-कृपा की आहट देती है: भटकने वाला दरबारी कवि बन उठता है, अचानक उस भीतरी घेरे में पहुँचा दिया जाता है जो दुनिया के लिए हर्ष की छवि गढ़ता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Bana in a quieter tent, seated by lamplight with palm leaves and stylus, the night camp visible beyond the flap
panels.action: By lamplight in a smaller tent, Banabhatta bends over palm leaves, stylus poised, while outside the flap the shadows of marching soldiers and tethered horses move across the canvas.

dialogue.text: From this point, we find Bana at work: crafting the Harshacharita, an ornate Sanskrit prose life of his patron, mingling his own past with the king’s origins.

i18n.hi: अब से हमें बना काम में मिलता है: ‘हर्षचरित’ लिखते हुए—अपने संरक्षक की जिंदगी पर सजावटी संस्कृत गद्य, जिसमें अपनी बीती और राजा की शुरुआत घुल जाती है।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot, showing visions from Bana’s mind: Pushyabhuti lineage, Harsha’s youth, battles, all faintly sketched around him as he writes
panels.action: Around the writing Banabhatta, faint images seem to rise—ancestral kings, a founding Pushyabhuti, Harsha in battle and council—like scenes forming in his imagination.

dialogue.text: He records legends of the Pushyabhuti line and Harsha’s rise. Later historians warn: these origin myths are not inscriptional fact but part of a crafted royal story.

i18n.hi: वह पुष्यभूति वंश और हर्ष के उभार की दंतकथाएँ दर्ज करता है। बाद के इतिहासकार टोकते हैं: ये उद्गम-कथाएँ शिलालेख जैसी ठोस सच्चाई नहीं, बल्कि गढ़ी हुई राज-कथा का हिस्सा हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bana with other courtiers and scholars, perhaps a chessboard-like layout on the floor, showing chaturanga pieces as he observes and absorbs details
panels.action: Banabhatta sits with other courtiers beside a board laid out with fourfold chaturanga pieces, watching a game intently as an officer gestures over the arrangement.

dialogue.text: In one famous passage, Bana mentions chaturanga, the fourfold battle array—elephants, chariots, horse and foot—evidence for early chess-like play, though not proof that Harsha invented it.

i18n.hi: एक मशहूर अंश में बना ‘चतुरंग’ का ज़िक्र करता है—चार अंगों वाली सेना: हाथी, रथ, घोड़े और पैदल—जो शतरंज जैसे खेल की पुरानी झलक देता है, पर ये साबित नहीं करता कि हर्ष ने ही खेल बनाया था।

panels.shot: split-focus shot: foreground on Bana’s hand writing ornate phrases, background a hazy vision of Harsha’s army marching, underlining how words shape power
panels.action: Banabhatta’s hand moves steadily across the palm leaf, while behind him, out of focus, ranks of armored soldiers pass by the tent entrance in steady file.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like Sheldon Pollock call this kind of Sanskrit prose a political language of the court—a way to stage power, not simple chronicle or neutral report.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान, जैसे शेल्डन पोलॉक, ऐसी संस्कृत गद्य को दरबार की ‘राजनीतिक भाषा’ कहते हैं—ताकत को मंच पर सजाने का जरिया, न कि सीधी इतिहास-लेख या निष्पक्ष रिपोर्ट।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bana presenting his finished manuscript to a circle of elite listeners, some nodding, some expressionless
panels.action: Banabhatta kneels as he offers his stacked palm-leaf manuscript to a group of seated nobles and officials, their faces a mix of approval, calculation, and polite blankness.

dialogue.text: Kaushik Roy and others read the Harshacharita as historical fiction with a factual core: battles and kings drawn from life, wrapped in elaborate praise and arranged to suit courtly taste.

i18n.hi: कौशिक रॉय और औरों की नज़र में ‘हर्षचरित’ तथ्य की गाँठ वाला ऐतिहासिक उपन्यास है: लड़ाइयाँ और राजा तो असली हैं, पर उन्हें शाही रुचि के मुताबिक, घुमावदार प्रशंसा में लपेटकर सजाया गया है।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium close-up of older Bana under a tree, manuscript in his lap, looking out toward the horizon where faint outlines of temples and cities appear
panels.action: An older Banabhatta sits beneath a broad tree with his manuscript in his lap, gazing toward a hazy horizon where the silhouettes of cities and temples seem to float in the heat.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta shows how a single writer at a king’s side can preserve an age—and how readers must walk carefully between his shining sentences to find the king, the world, and the poet himself.

i18n.hi: बनभट्ट दिखाता है कि राजा की छाती के पास बैठा एक अकेला लेखक पूरा युग बचा सकता है—और यह भी कि पाठक को उसकी चमकदार पंक्तियों के बीच सँभलकर चलना होगा, ताकि राजा, उसकी दुनिया और खुद कवि—तीनों को पहचान सके।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a wandering son of the soil crowned a king with words
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मिट्टी का भटकता बेटा ने राजा को शब्दों से मुकुट पहनाया
